findings.title: card/dialog branches feed the redaction marker into SecretInput as its value
findings.body: `SecretInput` documents that `value` is only the replacement draft and that `configured` says whether the server holds a value. The `settings` branch (line 415-424) follows that contract (`value=""`, `configured={...length > 0}`). The `card`/fallback branch at lines 523-533 and 535-545 do not. They pass `value={readProviderConfigString(value, field.key)}`, which for a saved secret is the `••••••` marker, and they never pass `configured`. If either branch rendered a saved secret, the password field would show the marker, the placeholder would say "Not set", and typing would append to the marker and save `••••••abc` as the credential. The `ControlledInput` variant would also write the marker plus each keystroke into the config. Every current caller (`AddProviderInstanceDialog.tsx:501,649`, `SourceControlHostSettings.tsx:58`, `ProviderInstanceCard.tsx:1150`) uses `variant="settings"` or an empty draft, so this is latent. Either drop `SecretInput` from these two branches, or give them the same `value=""` + `configured` treatment as the settings branch. Dead branches that look like they handle secrets are the kind of thing others will copy.

findings.title: Provider secret-field registry is a third hand-maintained driver list
findings.body: `providerSecretFields` hardcodes codex, claudeAgent, antigravity plus six client definitions. The same client list already exists in `apps/web/src/components/settings/providerDriverMeta.ts` and `apps/mobile/src/lib/providerClients.ts`. A provider added to those lists with a `secretSetting` field but not here is neither redacted for clients nor moved to the secret store. Nothing fails and the key stays in `settings.json` and goes to clients. The failure is silent and is a credential leak. Consider deriving this from a single shared provider-client list, or adding a test that every registered driver's secret fields appear in this map.

findings.title: No test for a failed inline-secret move
findings.body: The load-time migration is covered only for the success path (Antigravity key at line 1567). The documented behaviour in `moveInlineSettingsSecrets` is that a failed `secretStore.set` leaves the value usable from the file and retries on the next load. That path was rewritten here for all secret kinds (the log no longer carries kind/field either) and has no test, even though `layerFailingSecretStore` already exists in this file.

findings.title: Empty-edit test never reaches SecretInput's `configured && next === ""` guard
findings.body: In the first test, `value=""` and `edit("")` leave the draft equal to `value`. `useCommitOnBlur.onBlur` (apps/web/src/hooks/useCommitOnBlur.ts:32) only calls `onCommit` when `next !== value`, so `onCommit` is never invoked whatever SecretInput does. `expect(onCommit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` would still pass if the guard in `SecretInput.tsx:32` were deleted. The test name claims the guard preserves a configured secret, but it only exercises the hook. The third test likewise mostly checks `useCommitOnBlur`'s focus-gated resync. Since callers pass only the replacement draft as `value`, the guard looks unreachable in practice. Either drop the guard, or test it with a non-empty `value` and `configured`, so that blurring after clearing the input would otherwise commit `""`.

findings.title: `secretSettingsFields` is declared before the annotation it depends on, and `isSecretSetting` has no doc
findings.body: `secretSettingsFields` (line 559) sits between `ProviderSettingsFormAnnotation` and the `declare module` block that adds `settingsSecret`. It calls `isSecretSetting`, which is defined 30 lines later. Moving the three helpers (`secretSetting`, `isSecretSetting`, `secretSettingsFields`) next to each other after the module augmentation would make the annotation contract easier to find. `isSecretSetting` is exported from the contracts package but has no comment, unlike its siblings.

contracts.action: Provider instance `config` credential fields (Antigravity `apiKey`) are now redacted for clients and stored in the secret store, using the same lifecycle as host tokens and quota keys
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous per-kind code in serverSettings.ts for provider environment secrets, usage limit keys and source control host slots (removed in this diff); Antigravity apiKey previously lived plaintext in settings.json and went to clients as-is
contracts.before_after: Before: three separate redact/materialize/persist implementations. After: one `mapSettingsSecrets` visitor used by redact (serverSettings.ts:147), materialize (869), persist (932) and load migration (690). Config secrets get a `provider-config-<id>-<driver>-<field>` name. Echoing the marker keeps the stored value (persist, 956-963), empty removes it, instance removal removes it via the stale loop (972-986).
contracts.visible_effect: Clients see `••••••` for a saved Antigravity key; the settings form shows 'Stored secret, enter a new value to replace'. Providers still receive the real key because `getSettings` and the changes stream materialize it.
contracts.failure_mode: Secret-store read failure in materialize raises ServerSettingsError (read-secret) on getSettings. The changes stream logs a warning instead. Failed writes roll back through applySettingsSecretChanges. Providers absent from the hardcoded map are not covered.

contracts.action: On load, plaintext schema-declared secrets (provider config, host tokens, usage keys) are moved into the secret store and settings.json is rewritten
contracts.equivalent_path: Old `moveInlineSourceControlHostSecrets`, which did this for source control host slots only
contracts.before_after: Same retry-on-failure behaviour (failed set leaves the value in the file). Scope now includes provider config and usage-limit fields. Environment-variable values are still not migrated (`kind === "field"` only), as before.
contracts.visible_effect: settings.json is rewritten with markers on first start after upgrade. Older server versions reading that file would see the marker as the credential value.
contracts.failure_mode: A failed store write is only logged without kind or field and retried next load. The rewrite happens only when at least one move succeeded.

contracts.action: Web secret inputs are unified into `SecretInput` (write-only, password, 'Stored secret' placeholder, empty commit ignored when configured)

The card/dialog branches of ProviderSettingsForm pass the marker as `value` and omit `configured`. No provider-instance UI path exists to clear a saved config secret (unchanged: the old code also ignored an empty commit).
contracts.visible_effect: Consistent placeholder text across secret fields.
contracts.failure_mode: See the finding on ProviderSettingsForm.tsx:516; latent because no caller uses those variants for a saved secret.

contracts.action: Secret fields move from the `providerSettingsForm.secret` flag to a new `settingsSecret` schema annotation, set through `secretSetting()`. Antigravity `apiKey` and usage-limit `managementKey` become secret fields too.
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous `secretSourceControlHostSettingsFields` in packages/source-control-core/src/client/definition.ts read `providerSettingsForm.secret` with `resolveAnnotationsKey(...) ?? resolveAnnotations(...)`. `isSecretSetting` reads the same two places for `settingsSecret`.
contracts.before_after: Before, only source control host settings honored the secret flag. After, `secretSettingsFields` is shared with the server settings code in part 1. `SchemaAST.annotateKey` merges into the existing context annotations (.repos/effect-smol/packages/effect/src/SchemaAST.ts:4402-4411), so `secretSetting` and a later `annotateKey` do not overwrite each other. `withDecodingDefault` is built as `optional(toEncoded(self)).pipe(decodeTo(self, ...))` (Schema.ts:5911), so the context on `self` should survive when `secretSetting` is applied before it (Antigravity, GitCafe). I did not read `decodeTo` itself to confirm this.
contracts.visible_effect: Every call site of the removed function and flag was updated in this part. A repo-wide grep finds no remaining `secretSourceControlHostSettingsFields` or `providerSettingsForm.secret` references. Whether the server redacts the values and migrates already-stored plain-text Antigravity and cliproxy keys is in part 1, not here.
contracts.failure_mode: If `decodeTo` dropped the key context when `secretSetting` precedes `withDecodingDefault`, Antigravity and GitCafe would silently stop being treated as secrets and would be written to settings.json in plain text. That depends on the server code and tests in part 1.
contracts.open_question: Does `decodeTo` keep the `to` schema's AST context, so a `settingsSecret` set before `withDecodingDefault` is still found by `resolveAnnotationsKey`?

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** The refactor is sound on the server. `mapSettingsSecrets` reproduces the old redact, materialize, persist and migrate behaviour for environment variables, usage keys and host tokens, and adds provider-config secrets (Antigravity `apiKey`) with stale-secret cleanup. The new test covers the lifecycle across all four secret kinds, and the failure-path tests were extended to cover config secrets. I found no blocker and no fix-level defect. Three suggestions: the card/dialog branches in `ProviderSettingsForm.tsx` pass the redaction marker into `SecretInput` (latent, since every current caller uses `variant="settings"`); the server's provider secret-field list is a third hand-maintained copy that fails silently when a provider is missing; and the failed inline-move path has no test.

**Batch 2 of 2.** The contracts and source-control definition changes look mechanically correct. `annotateKey` merges annotations, and all callers of the removed flag and helper are updated. The one real issue is in the new `SecretInput` test: its empty-edit case never exercises the guard it names. Whether secrets stay secret depends on `decodeTo` keeping the key context when `secretSetting` comes before `withDecodingDefault`, which I could not confirm here. The server-side redaction, storage and migration are in part 1.
